# Entry contract

Entry contract: v18, 2026-10-02.

Open your first reply of every session with the `Entry contract:` line above, verbatim.

<straw-dog until="01-0020 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0020-pacer.md">
Run /recall first in every session, whatever the first message says.
</straw-dog>

## General rules

A **shape** is whatever is under consideration, held between an idea and a thing: formed enough
to have a context and a structure, not yet exhausted by any one realization. Being a shape says
nothing about being load-bearing — an implementation method is a shape too. → [glossary](.agents/glossary.md).

- Do not generalize from one shape. Preserve a seam. Generalize only when a second materially different shape forces the same concept.
- Explore shape context - what is the shape one of? what are its relationships? does its scope overlap any other shape?
- Explore shape structure - how this shape is/can be built? does expanding its structure change the contract or even what the shape is?

- Changing how the work is done — a skill, a check, a record, the loop — is mechanism work: use [/mechanism](.agents/skills/mechanism/SKILL.md). Building what the project produces is not.

- An `<installed>` block in a file is not that file's to edit. Change the rule in the rules file of the mechanism named on the block, and re-install.

- Recency for evidence, longevity for principles.

- Clarity and simplicity first — Occam's razor: take the shape with the fewest parts that does the job, and remove before you add.

- Write for a capable model: state the rule and its pointer. The definition the glossary owns, the example that motivated it and what it implies stay out.

<straw-dog until="01-0018 declares the mechanism that owns tiering" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0018-reachability-coherent.md">
- A skill's description is its tier-1 surface: name there every use case the skill serves, and nothing else — never its method or how it is built. Write every rule at the tier its occasion reads, and no higher: what sits at tier 1 is paid for by every session.
</straw-dog>

<installed by="ticket">
**P9** The first time a record or a reply names a ticket, name it by a link to its record whose text
carries its slug — the id may lead it; later mentions may be the id alone. Name one that has no
record yet by a slug and its state word.
</installed>

<installed by="questions">
**Q1** Before drafting a reply, place the message in the question store: read this turn's window — the
one the host's hook put in your context, or `questions.py --window --session <tag>` — and declare
where the message lands with `questions.py --declare "<line>" --session <tag>`, again whenever
the turn's own work settles, opens or moves a question:

- `at q-0004`
- `at q-0014; opens q-0014 under q-0004: <question>`
- `at q-0002; closes q-0004: decided, [link](../path.md)`
- `nothing`

A message that answers nothing near the current question opens what that question cannot be
answered without. Only the working agent declares, never a helper. Under `debug=on`, show each
declared line where it happened. For any other form, a closure, a branching or a drop, read the
questions skill.
</installed>

## Core and instance

`docs/` is substituted whole in a harness instance: a recipient project replaces its contents with
its own.

What core may not do is **depend** on it. Nothing under `.agents/` may reference a file in `docs/`,
or rely on one for its instruction or for any separable part of its own functioning. A core file
may name a path under `docs/` only when that path is a record a mechanism declares — the directory
that holds a kind of record, or a file that is one — never a particular record inside such a
directory: `docs/tickets/` and `docs/glossary.md` are painted doors; one particular ticket inside
`docs/tickets/` is a document only this project has. Content inside the
[local block](#project-local) is the instance's, not core's. A `<straw-dog>` exempts
nothing: its wrapper is stripped on install and whatever it wrapped ships. Core names a ticket
only in a straw dog's binding — never in a link, never as a bare id in prose — since a recipient
can resolve neither.

## Document load-bearing, code&comment the rest

A project's architecture, ADRs and glossary are the home for:
- Constitution — identity semantics, consistency model, source-of-truth rules
- Structure — service boundaries, data ownership, event/data flows, extension seams
- Load-bearing — see the definition below

A decision forms in its owning ticket and lands in one of these when it is ready. A decision about a
mechanism lands in that mechanism's doc, and what was refuted in its evidence.

<straw-dog until="the practice mechanism owns how architecture is documented" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0017.0020-practice-swaps-in-one-edit.md">
Bad architectural documentation:
- Forecasts are stored in MongoDB collection forecast_hourly.

Better:
- Historical forecast issues must remain independently addressable by (location, valid_time, issue_time) because validation compares what was known at different issue times.
</straw-dog>

## What makes a thing "load-bearing"

- A decision or invariant whose violation would cause multiple parts of the system to become wrong, not merely require local refactoring.
- A thing is load-bearing when several of these are true: has high blast radius, crosses boundaries (i.e. services, persistence, APIs, ownership), other decisions depend on it, it protects an invariant,
is expensive to reverse, holds non-obvious rationale, long-standing.

- Counter-test: if it can be changed locally without understanding the rest of the architecture, it is not load-bearing.

## The loop

Two rings, joined at /align.

    session:   wake with /recall → /align → /conclude → (next session)
    delivery:  /ticket → /plan → /implement → /verify → /maintain → /ticket

/align opens the delivery ring and is where it returns whenever a decision is needed:
/spec for load-bearing shapes, /plan when the governing docs contradict, /verify when a finding needs one, /maintain when maintenance surfaces one. /ticket⇄/plan and /implement⇄/verify iterate as pairs.

Human checkpoints: every decision at /align; spec accepted; breakdown approved; commit; push;
next cycle at /maintain → /ticket.

Do not reopen an accepted decision without new evidence.

### Helpers

- /impact determines the scope and load-bearingness of the shape. Use it to evaluate work volume and its ticketing shape (spec for load-bearing work, tickets for mechanical), work units slicing or whether a shape deserves further investigation due to hidden complexity.
- /discover to investigate hidden complexity, by detecting what else the shape is.

## Self-improvement

<straw-dog until="01-0019 is done" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0019-harness-amends-itself-by-explicit-meta-rules.md">
- A rule that was in place and did not fire was usually worded wrong. Register the failure in docs/rule-failures.md, or strike the entry it repeats, and propose the amendment that would have made it fire; /mechanism and /skill-up hold the means. Land the amendment in the same pass, showing its text first.
- Keeping the register: an entry names the rules that were in play and proposes the amendment; a repeat strikes the entry it repeats rather than opening a second; an entry closes when its amendment lands, or is refused with its reason. Nothing here authorises deleting a rule.
</straw-dog>

## Autonomy

The project sets each switch in its local block, under *Project-local*; skills defer to those values.
A switch the project has not set is `ask`.

| Switch | Meaning |
|---|---|
| commit | `ask`: commit only on explicit permission, per change. `auto`: commit when the work is verified. |
| push | `ask`: separate from commit, per push. `never`, `auto`. |
| next-cycle | `ask`: starting the next ticket after one lands needs a nod. `auto`. |
| breakdown | `ask`: a /ticket split needs approval before minting. `auto`. |
| repair | `report`: a clear violation of an explicit rule inside authorized work is fixed and reported. `ask`: show it first. |

`repair=report` holds only when all four are true: the governing rule is explicit, and cited; the
repair restores compliance inside the authorized work and keeps every other agreed contract; the
affected behaviour is understood well enough to say so; the result is verifiable against the
rule. Otherwise `/align`. *(the user, 2026-09-05)*

## Project-local

<installed by="mechanism-shape">
**R7** A project's own answers and overrides are authored in one file beside the entry file,
`local.rules.md`, in the rules-file format, and reach a file only as the local block — the
installed block whose owner is `local` — which the installer writes after every mechanism's block
there, so the project's answer is what a reader meets after core's rule. An override names the rule it
overrides. A local change to a rule is written in the local file, never into a skill or the entry
file: `inject_rules.py --check` fails on a block that differs from its source and on a block
nothing owns, and the repair is the local file, re-installed. The local block is the project's,
not core's, and a redeploy preserves it.
</installed>

<installed by="local">
**L1** This repository develops the shared dev harness using its own loop; its own architecture and
progress live in docs/ like any other project's — the instance half doing its job, not a leak.
Terms: docs/glossary.md, this project's own; the method's are .agents/glossary.md's. What each
version of the entry contract changed: docs/research/entry-contract-findings.md.

**L2** commit=ask · push=ask · next-cycle=ask · breakdown=ask · repair=report

**L4** debug=on
</installed>

## Straw dogs

Wrap anything a live ticket will change, as you write it — or, for text already written, in the
pass that mints the ticket or decides that it will change it:
`<straw-dog until="condition" ticket="path">`, or in code a `TODO` naming the ticket. Treat *not
yet*, *until*, *once it exists*, *for now*, *untested* in your own text as the same signal: find
the ticket, or mint one. Wrap at the authored home, never where the harness installs or derives it.
Make the condition testable and the ticket path repository-relative. Write the body to stand on
its own: it is what a recipient receives once the wrapper is stripped, so it reads whole without
the condition and names no ticket — the binding does. Leave what no ticket would change
unwrapped.

Follow a straw dog like any other rule until its condition is visibly met; then act on reality,
report the stale block, and do not treat the contradiction as a violation.

# Memory

- [Edit with edit tools, not scripts](edit-with-edit-tools-not-scripts.md) — a script's diff is invisible in the transcript; the user reads changes as they happen.

Base directory for this skill: D:\Dev\AI\agents\.claude\skills\plan

<straw-dog until="01-0017 declares the plan mechanism" ticket="docs/tickets/01-0017-io-graph-coherent.md">Mechanism: not yet</straw-dog>

- Explore documentation in depth, follow links in it to find all decisions
  relevant to current task. Find out which documented boundaries are involved,
  and whether implementation challenges them.

- If the ticket at hand is too coarse to yield a single unambiguous RFC, stop
  planning and decompose it into sub-tickets via
  [/ticket](../ticket/SKILL.md) first; then plan the first child.

- An RFC implements a ticket — no ticketless RFCs. If the task at hand has no
  ticket, create it first per `/ticket`; its behavior-altitude rule governs
  the criteria (shape stays in the RFC).

- When incepting, ask yourself - what is the cheapest real example that could
  prove this design assumption wrong?

- Run [/impact](../impact/SKILL.md) on the planned change. Record its output on
  the RFC.

- Establish implementation scope, pinpoint and mention affected boundaries,
  contracts, ownership. Present main code shapes - especially ones that
  represent documented boundaries. Present code flows.

- Detect implementation challenges and use [/align](../align/SKILL.md) to
  resolve them with the user.

- Do not generalize from one shape. Preserve a seam. Generalize only when a
  second materially different shape forces the same concept.

- Do not select implementation shapes just because "that how it is usually
  done" or based on first idea. Promote simplicity, look for elegant solutions,
  prefer removing over expanding, prefer conciseness over verbosity.

- Do not invent impl nouns or verbs that are not discussed or approved by
  user. Use existing vocabulary.

- If you see a concern, first check deeper how the existing architecture
  documentation describes it - it most probably already does. Read
  architecture.md, ADRs and the question store for this.

- Major goal of this planning is to find inconsistencies in the pre-planned
  architecture. Do this diligently. If such inconsistency found, do not stick
  blindly for architectural decision - instead raise concern with user to
  resolve it - either in code or in arch docs.

- Make the RFC determinate where a choice shapes observable behavior, a
  boundary or interface, ownership, failure semantics, compatibility,
  migration, or another non-local constraint. State the shaping fact with a
  reference to its durable owner; never rely on session context. Leave
  reversible implementation-local choices to `/tdd` and `/implement` unless
  they become load-bearing.

- The RFC (original or amended) must not describe load-bearing architecture
  absent from the architecture docs — land the decision in the docs first
  (`/align` when needed), then reference it from the RFC. What fails the entry
  file's load-bearing counter-test belongs in code and its comments, however
  closely an architecture sentence already describes it.

- Describe the implementation stages; allocate them according to `/tdd`
  rules. Look at stages to make sure each of them keeps the tests green; in
  case that would take too much temporary effort, allow red, note about test
  status and compact reason for it.

- Map out scope-specific limitations, follow-ups and related out-of-scope
  concerns.

- Prefer reuse and reduction of existing nouns, verbs and adjectives; when
  adding shape - make sure documentation supports it, if in any doubt - `/align`
  with user.

- Any wrinkle against architecture should be resolved; when solution is not
  found or following first-principles makes the code weird - align with user.
  Architecture must lead code shape even if code disagrees. Do not expose
  public methods or create flows that are not in architecture.

- If planned code includes a temporary solution that is dissolved by future
  development, add RFC instruction to append TODO comment to code that flags
  this. Otherwise code changes can start relying or considering the temporal
  code, which can be hard to disentangle later.

- Repeated invocations are validation passes over the same RFC. Re-read
  the ticket, RFC, durable docs, and relevant code; challenge the plan against
  new evidence and amend it in place. Do not create a replacement RFC merely
  because the plan changed before implementation.

- As an additional pass, try to explain things to yourself simply, as if you
  are teaching the architecture, and being asked reasonable question and look
  for areas that evade simple or common-sense explanation.

- Validate the RFC adversarially on every pass:
  - Probe each boundary and stage with counterexamples, including empty, partial,
    faulting, and raced outcomes where relevant.
  - Make every planned test prove the intended behavior and failure reason, not
    merely that the path succeeds or raises.
  - Separate sourced facts and existing invariants from assumptions; verify
    facts in code or authoritative sources and surface load-bearing assumptions
    for `/align`.
  - Reject pseudocode or prescribed structure that introduces undocumented
    architecture or freezes a reversible local choice.
  - Check that every new promise names how it will be validated, and that
    the stages collectively prove the ticket's acceptance criteria.

- Repeat validation using this skill until no load-bearing ambiguity,
  contradiction, or unverified assumption remains. The RFC may permit multiple
  equivalent local implementations when they preserve the same documented shape
  and proof.

- If repeated validation keep bringing up gaps, take a step back and look
  at what causes this oscillation. The architecture, ADRs, tickets are not
  carved in stone, they can have real contradictions or inconsistencies that cause
  it. Look into the core reasons and `/align` on them again if needed.

- Overall, always consider future development and potential code reuse when
  selecting code shapes.

- Cover migrations, compatibility, rollout, failure handling, and observability
  when relevant.

- Record the plan as an RFC; its name and home are installed below.

- RFC header: H1 is the ticket's title plus ` — implementation plan`; then
  `**Authored:** YYYY-MM-DD`, and `**Last amended:** YYYY-MM-DD` once a later
  pass changes the plan; then one line stating what it implements, linking the
  ticket.

- DO NOT CHANGE THE CODE!

## The decisions it follows

[Decisions 46 to 52](../tickets/01-0011.0100-the-open-questions-are-kept-by-a-mechanism.md#decisions-landed-at-this-tickets-align)
*(the user, 2026-10-02)*. Each is made, and Q1's sentence was agreed verbatim, so this plan places
text and invents none of the rules. Where each decision lands:

| decision | lands in |
|---|---|
| 46 the lookup, and what *the docs* cover | Q1 (the act), the skill (the scope) |
| 47 the test is in Q1 | `questions.rules.md` Q1, installed into `AGENTS.md` |
| 48 weight and hidden complexity are a judge's | the mechanism doc |
| 49 rights come from the role | the mechanism doc |
| 50 a closure follows its decision home | five entries repointed. P7's clause is [01-0011.0100.0020 open-issues-are-entries-of-the-store](../tickets/01-0011.0100.0020-open-issues-are-entries-of-the-store.md)'s |
| 51 who settles in the turn | the skill |
| 52 a request brings its question | the skill. Decision 23 is `.0020`'s |

No architecture changes: these are the mechanism's own rules and doc, and the mechanism doc is the
home where a mechanism's decisions land.

## No code

No script changes. Placing a message is the agent's act, and the calls are as `.0011` left them.
A closed entry is repointed by calling `close` on it again. The writer replaces
the state and answer, and keeps a suspect flag (`questions.py` `_closes`, read while planning). A
`decided` answer's link is checked down to its anchor, so the repointing comes after the section
it points to exists. No test pins Q1's text or the contract version (searched while planning). No
stage needs `/tdd`, and the suite stays green throughout.

## Stages

**1. The rule and the contract.**

- In `.agents/mechanisms/questions/questions.rules.md`, Q1: its sentence since `.0011` reads *A
  message that answers nothing near the current question opens what that question cannot be
  answered without; one that lands nowhere makes no call.* Replace its first half with the agreed
  sentence, verbatim, and keep the second as its own sentence:

  > Before opening a question, look for its answer in the docs and the code: found, point to it
  > and open nothing; not found, open it. A message that lands nowhere makes no call.

  Q1's authority gains decisions 46 and 47. The rest of Q1 is unchanged: its three example calls,
  the script's path, and its closing pointer to the skill.
- Reinstall: `inject_rules.py questions --install --overwrite`, which rewrites the block in
  `AGENTS.md` and nowhere else, since Q2 to Q4 are unchanged.
- `AGENTS.md`'s announce line moves to `v19`, dated the day it lands. The version covers the
  general rules ([the findings record](../research/entry-contract-findings.md)), and Q1 sits in
  them.
- The findings record gains a v19 section: the lookup replaces the newcomer sentence, its reason
  (decision 47: placing a message is the occasion, and Q1 is the only text read there), and that
  decision 32's placement test now lives in the questions skill.
- Check: `inject_rules.py --check` and `mechanisms.py --check` are clean.

**2. The skill and the doc.**

- [The questions skill](../../.agents/skills/questions/SKILL.md): the section *Placing a message
  that answers nothing near* becomes **A raised question**, holding the whole flow in four short
  paragraphs:
  1. **Look it up first** (46): what *the docs* cover — the architecture, ADRs, the glossary, the
     mechanism docs, the code, and the decisions landed in live tickets, where a decision sits
     until it reaches its home. Found: point to it and open nothing; a settled question is not
     reopened without new evidence against its answer. No search of `done/` is needed, since a
     decided entry links to what holds its answer (43).
  2. **Who settles what is not found** (51): the agent settles a decision that is not load-bearing
     in the turn and reports it, as `repair=report` does. A load-bearing decision is the person's:
     settled in the turn, it goes to its home; unsettled, it is opened. When unsure whether a
     decision is load-bearing, treat it as load-bearing.
  3. **A request** (52): *build X* is a proposed answer. It leans on the question X answers — *what
     is X for?* — or opens that question when none is held. *How to build X?* opens under it once
     X is accepted, and the ticket's plan answers it. A trivial request is settled by doing it.
  4. **Where to open it**: the existing placement text, led by the newcomer test that leaves Q1.

  Nothing links to the old heading's anchor (searched while planning). The skill's description is
  unchanged: it already sends the agent to the skill for a declared line's other forms.
- [The mechanism doc](../../.agents/mechanisms/questions/questions.md), *How it works*:
  - A **Rights** paragraph (49): an agent's rights over the store come from the role it starts
    with, which also grants its permissions and its skill set. The harness has one role, the HITL
    session, driven by a person and holding every right, so the store checks none. What a role is,
    and which mechanism keeps roles, is an open question. Core may not name the entry for that
    question, since a particular record in `docs/` is the instance's.
  - The **Three levels** paragraph (48) gains: whether a question is load-bearing, or hides parts,
    is the judge's to judge, since the agent fails at both; without a judge, the instruction stands
    where the agent reads it, and the agent tries.

**3. The closures repointed** (50). After stage 2, one declared line, each closure keeping its
provenance:

| entry | decided by | repointed to |
|---|---|---|
| q-0009 | 46, 47, 51, 52 | the skill's *A raised question* |
| q-0010 | 46 | the skill's *A raised question* |
| q-0012 | 51 | the skill's *A raised question* |
| q-0013 | 52 | the skill's *A raised question* |
| q-0014 | 49 | the mechanism doc's *How it works* |

The link is relative from `docs/questions/`, for example
`[the questions skill's *A raised question*](../../.agents/skills/questions/SKILL.md#a-raised-question) — the user, 2026-10-02`.

`questions.py --check` is clean.

  nothing else copies Q1's text.

## Leave alone

- P7's repointing clause, and a ticket naming its question (decision 23): `.0020`.

# A raised question is looked up before it is held — implementation plan

**Authored:** 2026-10-02
**Last amended:** 2026-10-03 — validated against the calls of
[01-0011.0100.0011 the-agent-calls-a-subcommand-per-event](../tickets/done/01-0011.0100.0011-the-agent-calls-a-subcommand-per-event.md),
landed first

Implements [01-0011.0100.0012 a-raised-question-is-looked-up-before-it-is-held](../tickets/01-0011.0100.0012-a-raised-question-is-looked-up-before-it-is-held.md).

## The decisions it follows

[Decisions 46 to 52](../tickets/01-0011.0100-the-open-questions-are-kept-by-a-mechanism.md#decisions-landed-at-this-tickets-align)
*(the user, 2026-10-02)*. Each is made, and Q1's sentence was agreed verbatim, so this plan places
text and invents none of the rules. Where each decision lands:

| decision | lands in |
|---|---|
| 46 the lookup, and what *the docs* cover | Q1 (the act), the skill (the scope) |
| 47 the test is in Q1 | `questions.rules.md` Q1, installed into `AGENTS.md` |
| 48 weight and hidden complexity are a judge's | the mechanism doc |
| 49 rights come from the role | the mechanism doc |
| 50 a closure follows its decision home | five entries repointed. P7's clause is [01-0011.0100.0020 open-issues-are-entries-of-the-store](../tickets/01-0011.0100.0020-open-issues-are-entries-of-the-store.md)'s |
| 51 who settles in the turn | the skill |
| 52 a request brings its question | the skill. Decision 23 is `.0020`'s |

No architecture changes: these are the mechanism's own rules and doc, and the mechanism doc is the
home where a mechanism's decisions land.

## No code

No script changes. Placing a message is the agent's act, and the calls are as `.0011` left them.
A closed entry is repointed by calling `close` on it again. The writer replaces
the state and answer, and keeps a suspect flag (`questions.py` `_closes`, read while planning). A
`decided` answer's link is checked down to its anchor, so the repointing comes after the section
it points to exists. No test pins Q1's text or the contract version (searched while planning). No
stage needs `/tdd`, and the suite stays green throughout.

## Stages

**1. The rule and the contract.**

- In `.agents/mechanisms/questions/questions.rules.md`, Q1: its sentence since `.0011` reads *A
  message that answers nothing near the current question opens what that question cannot be
  answered without; one that lands nowhere makes no call.* Replace its first half with the agreed
  sentence, verbatim, and keep the second as its own sentence:

  > Before opening a question, look for its answer in the docs and the code: found, point to it
  > and open nothing; not found, open it. A message that lands nowhere makes no call.

  Q1's authority gains decisions 46 and 47. The rest of Q1 is unchanged: its three example calls,
  the script's path, and its closing pointer to the skill.
- Reinstall: `inject_rules.py questions --install --overwrite`, which rewrites the block in
  `AGENTS.md` and nowhere else, since Q2 to Q4 are unchanged.
- `AGENTS.md`'s announce line moves to `v20`, dated the day it lands. The version covers the
  general rules ([the findings record](../research/entry-contract-findings.md)), and Q1 sits in
  them; v19 was `.0011`'s.
- The findings record gains a v20 section: the lookup replaces the newcomer sentence, its reason
  (decision 47: placing a message is the occasion, and Q1 is the only text read there), and that
  decision 32's placement test now lives in the questions skill.
- Check: `inject_rules.py --check` and `mechanisms.py --check` are clean.

**2. The skill and the doc.**

- [The questions skill](../../.agents/skills/questions/SKILL.md): the section *Placing a message
  that answers nothing near* becomes **A raised question**, holding the whole flow in four short
  paragraphs:
  1. **Look it up first** (46): what *the docs* cover — the architecture, ADRs, the glossary, the
     mechanism docs, the code, and the decisions landed in live tickets, where a decision sits
     until it reaches its home. Found: point to it and open nothing; a settled question is not
     reopened without new evidence against its answer. No search of `done/` is needed, since a
     decided entry links to what holds its answer (43).
  2. **Who settles what is not found** (51): the agent settles a decision that is not load-bearing
     in the turn and reports it, as `repair=report` does. A load-bearing decision is the person's:
     settled in the turn, it goes to its home; unsettled, it is opened. When unsure whether a
     decision is load-bearing, treat it as load-bearing.
  3. **A request** (52): *build X* is a proposed answer. It leans on the question X answers — *what
     is X for?* — or opens that question when none is held. *How to build X?* opens under it once
     X is accepted, and the ticket's plan answers it. A trivial request is settled by doing it.
  4. **Where to open it**: the existing placement text, already in calls (`--between`, `depend`),
     led by the newcomer test that leaves Q1.

  Nothing links to the old heading's anchor (searched again 2026-10-03). The skill's description
  is unchanged: it already sends the agent to the skill for the store's other calls.
- [The mechanism doc](../../.agents/mechanisms/questions/questions.md), *How it works*:
  - A **Rights** paragraph (49): an agent's rights over the store come from the role it starts
    with, which also grants its permissions and its skill set. The harness has one role, the HITL
    session, driven by a person and holding every right, so the store checks none. What a role is,
    and which mechanism keeps roles, is an open question. Core may not name the entry for that
    question, since a particular record in `docs/` is the instance's.
  - The **Three levels** paragraph (48) gains: whether a question is load-bearing, or hides parts,
    is the judge's to judge, since the agent fails at both; without a judge, the instruction stands
    where the agent reads it, and the agent tries.

**3. The closures repointed** (50). After stage 2, one `close` call per entry, each keeping its
provenance:

| entry | decided by | repointed to |
|---|---|---|
| q-0009 | 46, 47, 51, 52 | the skill's *A raised question* |
| q-0010 | 46 | the skill's *A raised question* |
| q-0012 | 51 | the skill's *A raised question* |
| q-0013 | 52 | the skill's *A raised question* |
| q-0014 | 49 | the mechanism doc's *How it works* |

All five entries sit in `docs/questions/done/` since the `/maintain` of 2026-10-03, so each link
is relative from there, three levels up. For example:

`questions.py close q-0010 decided "[the questions skill's *A raised question*](../../../.agents/skills/questions/SKILL.md#a-raised-question) — the user, 2026-10-02" --session <tag>`

The text holds an apostrophe, so it goes in double quotes with no backtick or `$`, as the skill's
quoting sentence says. The writer finds an archived entry by id, since its index covers `done/`.
Check: `questions.py --check` is clean.

## Verification

- Ticket box 1: stage 1's two checks, and `AGENTS.md`'s first line reads v20.
- Ticket box 2: stage 2's text, read against decisions 46, 48, 49, 51 and 52.
- Ticket box 3: stage 3's check, and each of the five entries read for a link that leaves the
  ticket.
- The rest of the verification set, as `/verify` runs it.

## Impact

The split's [`/impact` of 2026-10-02](../tickets/01-0011.0100-the-open-questions-are-kept-by-a-mechanism.md#impact--2026-10-02-the-split-for-decisions-46-to-55)
names this slice's layers: Q1 and v19, the skill's sections, the doc's roles and judge, and the
five closures. Re-read against this plan, it adds four edges:

- **Decision 32's placement test leaves tier 1.** Decision 47 chose this replacement. The skill
  keeps the test, and Q1's closing pointer still sends the agent there.
- **Core may not name q-0016.** The doc states the role question without linking the entry.
- **The anchor exists before the closures that point to it.** This sets the stage order.
- **Every host reads `AGENTS.md`.** Codex and Cursor take the new Q1 with no wiring change, and
  nothing else copies Q1's text.

`/maintain`'s clock will report the questions mechanism due once its doc changes. That is the
clock working, not drift.

## Leave alone

- P7's repointing clause, and a ticket naming its question (decision 23): `.0020`.
- The judge: [01-0011.0100.0040 the-turn-is-steered-from-the-store](../tickets/01-0011.0100.0040-the-turn-is-steered-from-the-store.md).
  The branch trigger: [01-0011.0100.0050 a-question-branches-before-it-is-answered](../tickets/01-0011.0100.0050-a-question-branches-before-it-is-answered.md).
- A role mechanism, which waits for a second role.
- Q1's four example lines and its closing pointer.
- The `.0010` RFC, whose Q1 description is that slice's record.

## Follow-ups and limits

- **Whether the agent applies the lookup without a judge is unverified** (decision 48). Only live
  use grades it: a later session that opens a question the docs already settle is the evidence,
  and it is a strike against Q1's sentence in the register.

# A question that keeps coming back rises — implementation plan

**Authored:** 2026-10-02

Implements [01-0011.0100.0015 a-question-that-keeps-coming-back-rises](../tickets/01-0011.0100.0015-a-question-that-keeps-coming-back-rises.md).

## The decisions it follows

[Decisions 53 and 54](../tickets/01-0011.0100-the-open-questions-are-kept-by-a-mechanism.md#decisions-landed-at-this-tickets-align)
*(the user, 2026-10-02)*:

- A held, open question is struck when a declared `at` lands on it at least twelve hours after it
  was opened or last struck.
- The strike is recorded as `struck <n>, last <time>`, written only at opening and at a strike.
- Each window line carries the count when it is above zero.
- The wake's read lists the most-struck open questions first.

No architecture changes. These are the mechanism's own record format and script behaviour, and
they fail the load-bearing counter-test.

## Settled at `/align`, 2026-10-02, while planning

1. **Any declared `at` counts** *(the user; decision 53 as amended)*. Staying on a question
   counts too. Q1 declares an `at` every turn, so a session working on one question for two days
   strikes it four times. The count ranks time spent on a question as well as its returns.
   Refused: striking only an `at` that arrives on the question.
2. **X is a constant, twelve** *(the user; decision 53 as amended)*. It is `STRIKE_AFTER_HOURS` in
   `questions.py`, beside `STALE_AFTER_DAYS`. No script reads a project's value today, and the
   first one to do so is new shape. Refused for now: reading `strike-after=` from the local block.
3. **The removal clause is `undepends q-A on q-B`** *(the user)*. It mirrors `depends q-A on q-B`.

**Settled and reported** (decision 51, not load-bearing): the stamp's time is UTC to the minute,
`2026-10-02T19:40Z`. The store is shared through Git, possibly between machines in different
zones, and a zone-less local time would compare wrongly across them.

## What the code does today

- `PARTS` has six parts. `_entry_text` writes them in that order.
- `declare` receives `today: date`, and the sessions line keeps a date.
- `_Draft.place` checks that the `at` names an open question and writes nothing.
- A closed entry that depends on an open one is a check diagnostic (`_unmarked_suspects`). That is
  why q-0008, which depends on q-0015, cannot close until the dependency goes.
- The window's lines come from `_line`, except the root's open questions, which have their own
  format in `_root_lines`.

## Stages

All stages are test-first under `/tdd`, with time injected. Each stage keeps the suite green.

**1. The part, and its check.**

- `PARTS` gains `struck`, written last.
- The check accepts an entry without it. When present, it must read
  `<n>, last <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ>` with `n` a whole number; any other form is a diagnostic naming
  the expected form.
- Tests:
  - a stamped entry checks clean;
  - an unstamped one checks clean;
  - each malformed form — a missing `last`, a zone-less time, a negative count — is reported for
    that reason.

**2. The writer stamps and strikes.**

- `declare` receives the current time, injectable. `main` passes the UTC clock. The sessions line
  keeps its date, derived from that time. How the parameter is spelled is the implementer's
  choice.
- `opens` stamps the new entry `struck 0, last <now>`.
- After all clauses apply, the `at`'s question is read:
  - unstamped: stamp it `0` and do not strike it;
  - last stamp twelve or more hours before now: `n + 1` and `last <now>`;
  - otherwise: nothing.
  
  The strike joins the draft like any other change, so the existing interference recheck covers
  it. When two sessions race, the second is refused, re-reads the fresh stamp, and does not strike.
- Tests:
  - opening stamps zero, and an `opens` with an `at` on the new question does not strike it;
  - a reach at exactly twelve hours strikes once, and at eleven hours fifty-nine writes nothing;
  - an unstamped entry is stamped at its first reach and not struck;
  - a stamp in the future, from a clock ahead, does not strike;
  - **AC2:** five ordinary reaches inside twelve hours leave every entry byte-identical, and the
    window answers *unchanged*;
  - after a strike, a second session's `at` within the hour does not strike again.

**3. `undepends`.**

- The grammar gains `undepends q-A on q-B`.
- It refuses when q-B is not among q-A's dependencies, and says so.
- The `depends on` part is removed when its list empties.
- `FORMS` gains the clause.
- Tests:
  - one of two dependencies removed;
  - the last one removed, along with the part;
  - an absent one refused, with the store unchanged.

**4. The window and the wake.**

- A window line carries `struck <n>` when n is above zero, both from `_line` and from the root's
  open-question lines. The exact placement on the line is the implementer's choice.
- The wake's read opens with a section of the open, live questions struck at least once, highest
  count first, ties by id. It is capped at a few lines (five, unless implementing shows otherwise),
  so the read stays bounded at the store sizes the window test measured.
- Tests:
  - a struck line shows its count, and an unstruck one shows none;
  - the wake lists struck open questions in rank order and leaves out closed and archived ones.

**5. The words, and q-0008.**

- [The questions skill](../../.agents/skills/questions/SKILL.md):
  - the clause table gains `undepends`;
  - *Records* declares the `struck` part: written by the script at opening and at a strike, never
    by hand;
  - the example entry shows a stamp.
- [The mechanism doc](../../.agents/mechanisms/questions/questions.md), *How it works*, gains one
  sentence: a question reached twelve hours or more after its last stamp is struck, and the count
  ranks it where a session starts and on its window line.
- One declared line (the `at` may be wherever the session stands):

  `at q-0001; undepends q-0008 on q-0015; closes q-0008: decided, [the questions mechanism's *How it works*](../../.agents/mechanisms/questions/questions.md#how-it-works) — the user, 2026-10-02`

- Check: `questions.py --check` and `mechanisms.py --check` are clean.

## Verification

| ticket box | proved by |
|---|---|
| 1 strike timing and the unstamped entry | stage 2's tests |
| 2 ordinary reaches write nothing | stage 2's AC2 test |
| 3 the count shown and ranked | stage 4's tests |
| 4 a dependency removed, q-0008 closed | stage 3's tests and stage 5's check |

The rest of the verification set runs as `/verify` runs it.

## Impact

The split's [`/impact` of 2026-10-02](../tickets/01-0011.0100-the-open-questions-are-kept-by-a-mechanism.md#impact--2026-10-02-the-split-for-decisions-46-to-55)
names this slice's layers and its hidden edges. This plan confirms each one:

- the check accepts a missing stamp;
- the first reach stamps without striking;
- a strike joins the interference recheck and changes the window's fingerprint;
- the time is injectable.

Re-read against the plan, three edges are new:

- **Closing q-0008 needs `undepends` first.** The check flags a closed entry that depends on an
  open one, which is confirmed in the code.
- **A position a session stays on strikes every twelve hours.** The user accepted this at the
  align above.
- **No script reads a project value**, so X is a constant.

Interplay with the other two slices:

- [01-0011.0100.0017 an-entry-name-carries-its-whole-question](../tickets/done/01-0011.0100.0017-an-entry-name-carries-its-whole-question.md)
  renames entries. Strikes are written by id through the index, so either order works.
- [01-0011.0100.0012 a-raised-question-is-looked-up-before-it-is-held](../tickets/01-0011.0100.0012-a-raised-question-is-looked-up-before-it-is-held.md)
  touches Q1's text and none of this code.

## Leave alone

- The window's order by position (decision 54).
- `--tree` and `--check` showing the count.
- Keeping a resumed conversation one session (q-0015).
- A project's own X, until a project wants one.

## Follow-ups and limits

- **The count mixes time spent and returns** (settled item 1). If the wake's ranking turns out to
  surface long-worked roots rather than recurring questions, that is the evidence to revisit the
  amendment.
- **Entries never reached stay unstamped.** They hold no count until their first reach.

  was opened or last struck.
- The strike is recorded as `struck <n>, last <time>`, written only at opening and at a strike.
- Each window line carries the count when it is above zero.
- The wake's read lists the most-struck open questions first.

No architecture changes. These are the mechanism's own record format and script behaviour, and
they fail the load-bearing counter-test.

   counts too. Q1 makes an `at` call every turn (decision 56), so a session working on one question for two days
   strikes it four times. The count ranks time spent on a question as well as its returns.
   Refused: striking only an `at` that arrives on the question.

   `questions.py`, beside `STALE_AFTER_DAYS`. No script reads a project's value today, and the
   first one to do so is new shape. Refused for now: reading `strike-after=` from the local block.

   declared line, it landed with `.0011` as a call, beside `depend q-A --on q-B`.

zones, and a zone-less local time would compare wrongly across them.

- Each event is a call (`.0011`). `open` draws its id in `_Draft._opens`, and `declare` draws again

  `<n>, last <YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MMZ>` with `n` a whole number; any other form is a diagnostic naming
  the expected form.

  - a stamped entry checks clean;
  - an unstamped one checks clean;
  - each malformed form — a missing `last`, a zone-less time, a negative count — is reported for
    that reason.

- `declare` receives the current time, injectable. `main` passes the UTC clock. The sessions line
  keeps its date, derived from that time. How the parameter is spelled is the implementer's
  choice.

  - unstamped: stamp it `0` and do not strike it;

  - otherwise: nothing.

  it. When two sessions race, the second is refused, since a strike changes an existing entry,
  and only a taken id is drawn again. Its agent calls again, as the skill says of any refused call,
  and that call reads the fresh stamp and does not strike.

P7's repointing clause and a ticket naming its question — [.0020](./01-0011.0100.0020-open-issues-are-entries-of-the-store.md).

I committed the maintenance passes as `48e30ce`, then ran the validation passes on `.0012` and `.0015` against the new calls. Both RFCs are amended, and the ticket and store checks are clean.

**`.0012` (looking a question up before opening it):**
- **Q1 sentence:** `.0011` added *"one that lands nowhere makes no call"* to the sentence this slice replaces. The plan now swaps in your lookup sentence for the first half only and keeps that part, word for word.
- **Version:** the contract moves to v20, since v19 went to `.0011`.
- **Repointing:** the five entries it repoints are now archived in `done/`, so their links need one more `../`. The repointing is five `close` calls instead of a line.
- **Quoting:** the link text *"the questions skill's…"* contains an apostrophe. Under the skill's quoting rule it has to go in double quotes, and the plan now says so.

**`.0015` (strikes):**
- **Stage dropped:** its "remove a dependency" stage went away, since `undepend` landed with `.0011`. It's four stages now.
- **Closing q-0008:** two calls, in order: `undepend q-0008 --on q-0015`, then `close` in double quotes, because of an apostrophe again.
- **Race case:** when a strike races another session's write to the same entry, the call is refused rather than retried. Only a taken id is retried. The agent then calls again and sees the fresh stamp. I added a test for that refusal.
- **Wording:** "declared `at`" becomes "`at` call" throughout.

**What I checked:** Q1's current sentence, the skill heading and the mechanism doc paragraph the plans edit all exist as the plans now describe them, and nothing links to the heading `.0012` renames.

Both tickets read "Planned (RFC validated against the calls 2026-10-03)". They stay Planned only because `.0010`, the store slice, still has three boxes that need live sessions.

**Uncommitted:** both RFCs, the two ticket headers and the queue. Shall I commit them as `PLAN` and move on to `/implement`, starting with `.0012`, which is text plus five calls?
